_note: Real lunar orbiters for the 'your design most resembles...' comparison. Only figures copied from a cited NASA source are stored. Entries that say 'confirm' must be checked against the NASA PDF before the demo.

real_missions.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)

launch_mass_kg.source: NASA LRO/LCROSS Press Kit, June 2009 (archived copy: https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/web/20090922191046/http:/lro.gsfc.nasa.gov/images/LRO_LCROSS_presskit.pdf). Figures read from Spaceflight Now's reproduction of the press kit text (https://spaceflightnow.com/atlas/av020/090610lro.html) because the PDF itself could not be opened; confirm against the PDF page before the demo. Launch mass 1,916 kg. Confirmed by the team against the NASA press kit, 14 Nov 2026.

dry_mass_kg.source: NASA LRO/LCROSS Press Kit, June 2009 (archived copy: https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/web/20090922191046/http:/lro.gsfc.nasa.gov/images/LRO_LCROSS_presskit.pdf). Figures read from Spaceflight Now's reproduction of the press kit text (https://spaceflightnow.com/atlas/av020/090610lro.html) because the PDF itself could not be opened; confirm against the PDF page before the demo. Dry mass 1,018 kg. Confirmed by the team against the NASA press kit, 14 Nov 2026.

orbit.value: Polar, about 50 km altitude (base mission); later 30 x 216 km
orbit.source: NASA NSSDCA LRO record and NAIF LRO SPICE catalog (insthost.cat): base mission 50 +/- 20 km, 30 x 216 km low-maintenance orbit for commissioning and extended mission.

primary_lifetime_months.source: NASA NSSDCA LRO record: one-year base mission in a polar orbit.

real_missions.instruments_source: NASA LRO/LCROSS Press Kit, June 2009 lists LROC, LOLA, LEND, LAMP, Diviner, CRaTER and Mini-RF. Confirmed by the team against the NASA press kit, 14 Nov 2026.

mission_orbit_alt_km.source: NAIF LRO SPICE catalog (insthost.cat): base mission altitude 50 +/- 20 km. https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/pds/data/lro-l-spice-6-v1.0/lrosp_1000/catalog/insthost.cat

real_missions.name: Lunar Prospector

launch_mass_kg.source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Prospector page, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunarprosp.html (last updated 28 Jan 2022), accessed 14 Nov 2026. Launch mass 296 kg fully fueled.

dry_mass_kg.source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Prospector page, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunarprosp.html (last updated 28 Jan 2022), accessed 14 Nov 2026. Dry mass 158 kg. An older NASA page (1997) and Wikipedia give 126 kg, so the sources disagree; the current NSSDCA page is used. Confirm before the demo.

orbit.value: Circular polar, about 100 km altitude, 118 minute period (later 40 km, then 30 km)
orbit.source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Prospector page, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunarprosp.html (last updated 28 Jan 2022), accessed 14 Nov 2026.

mission_orbit_alt_km.source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Prospector page, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunarprosp.html (last updated 28 Jan 2022), accessed 14 Nov 2026. Also NASA PDS mission catalog: 100 +/- 20 km mapping orbit.

primary_lifetime_months.source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Prospector page, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunarprosp.html (last updated 28 Jan 2022), accessed 14 Nov 2026. The nominal mission ended after one year; the full mission lasted 19 months.

real_missions.instruments_source: NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Prospector page, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunarprosp.html (last updated 28 Jan 2022), accessed 14 Nov 2026.

real_missions.name: Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter (KPLO / Danuri)
real_missions.agency: KARI (Korea), with NASA payload and support

launch_mass_kg.source: NASA KPLO/Danuri Launch Press Kit, August 2022 (NASA-branded PDF hosted at https://shadowcam.im-ldi.com/KPLO_english_press_kit.pdf), accessed 14 Nov 2026. Quick Facts: weight 678 kg. The press kit gives no dry mass, so none is stored.

orbit.source: NASA KPLO/Danuri Launch Press Kit, August 2022 (NASA-branded PDF hosted at https://shadowcam.im-ldi.com/KPLO_english_press_kit.pdf), accessed 14 Nov 2026. Lunar Orbit Insertion section.

mission_orbit_alt_km.source: NASA KPLO/Danuri Launch Press Kit, August 2022 (NASA-branded PDF hosted at https://shadowcam.im-ldi.com/KPLO_english_press_kit.pdf), accessed 14 Nov 2026.

primary_lifetime_months.source: NASA KPLO/Danuri Launch Press Kit, August 2022 (NASA-branded PDF hosted at https://shadowcam.im-ldi.com/KPLO_english_press_kit.pdf), accessed 14 Nov 2026. Quick Facts: one year primary mission and possible extended mission.

real_missions.instruments_source: NASA KPLO/Danuri Launch Press Kit, August 2022 (NASA-branded PDF hosted at https://shadowcam.im-ldi.com/KPLO_english_press_kit.pdf), accessed 14 Nov 2026. The six payloads onboard KPLO.
